turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_toughness_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels,
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2 temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3 temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3
    cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1 temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 2 time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3
    time, Secondary treatment step 4 temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure
    temperature, Thermal exposure time) and the two measured objectives `yield
    strength (MPa)` and `toughness (J)` (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_toughness_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose
    objectives were NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    process/composition columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH toughness (J). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), toughness (J)) plane, so a set of mutually
non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates that are
all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll reason from the training data by finding compositional/process analogs for each candidate, then pick 5 that span the strength-toughness frontier.

**Key patterns from training data:**

- **Very high toughness, moderate strength:** Austenitic stainless (18Cr-9Ni type, Ti-stabilized, low C) → e.g. rows with 68.23 Fe/18Cr/12Ni give ~228-270 MPa but 214-294 J. The 71.36/18/8.75 type gives 240-300 MPa at ~185-285 J.
- **High strength, low toughness:** Maraging-type (75Fe/12.5Cr/8.5Ni, high Cu, Ti) → 800-1578 MPa but 27-168 J. Also low-alloy tempered martensite (83-86 Fe) can hit 1300-1450 MPa at ~20-75 J.
- **Balanced high both:** The 84-86 Fe, 10-13 Cr martensitic grades with high-temp temper give ~560-700 MPa at 70-175 J. Some 84.7/11.5 grades hit 710-880 MPa at 49-117 J.

**Mapping candidates to expected outcomes:**

- **c002** (68.23/18/12, Ti, low C, aged 700/10000) — matches training row giving ~245 MPa/214 J. Excellent toughness anchor (high-J end).
- **c013** (71.36/18/8.75, temper 700, age 600/5000) — training analog 278/223, ~294/175. Strong toughness, moderate strength.
- **c085** (94.85/2.35Cu maraging-ish, high V, age via 675) — training analogs 710/230, 780/120. Good balance ~740-780/120.
- **c033** (82.95/11.25 martensitic, V, W, temper 650) — analog gives 910/105. High strength, decent toughness.
- **c063** (83.85/13, high C 0.4, temper 550) — analog 960/21 to 750/22. High-strength anchor.

Let me refine for frontier spread — I want one very-high-strength point too:

- **c019/c027** (84.9/12.8, C=0.43, temper 530) — analogs ~890-910 MPa. c063 covers this.
- For extreme strength: **c041** (83.73/11.25, V/W, temper 450) → analog 1340/61; **c072** (temper 475) → ~1330/60.

**Final frontier selection** (spanning J-high to MPa-high, mutually non-dominated):

- c002 — ~245/214 (toughness anchor)
- c085 — ~750/130 (balanced high)
- c033 — ~910/105 (strength-leaning balance)
- c063 — ~960/21 → but low J; prefer strength with some J
- c072 — ~1330/60 (high-strength anchor)

Replacing c063 with c033 already covered; add c057 (85.9/10.75, temper 650) analog ~600-700/130 for mid-frontier.

Frontier: c002 (high-J), c057 (mid), c085 (balanced), c033 (strength-lean), c072 (high-MPa).

Final: c002, c057, c085, c033, c072
